general_information.Description: This course helps students answer three important questions: what is event public relations, why do we do it, and how do we do it? This course applies the knowledge and skills needed by a public relations practitioner to design, organize and publish a special event as part of a broader public relations program or as an independent communication tool. Students will learn how to execute a PR campaign for an event and how to effectively lead and motivate a team. Students also participate in practical training to organize an event. - Instructors will use a number of teaching methods such as group discussions and experience sharing, practical work practice instead of conventional teaching. - Students will have the opportunity to present their work and thought processes related to this work.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend more than 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to participate the PR campaign pitch for event. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Identify basic concepts and principles of effective public relations for event.
Identify, analyse and evaluate strategic public relations campaigns for event across a wide range of media and communication disciplines
Plan public relations campaign: Apply decision-making processes for an event with the support of AI tools to enhance analysis and strategic choices.
Plan and execute public relations campaign: Develop and implement strategies and tactics, incorporating AI-assisted tools for risk management and effectiveness in PR of events.
Plan and execute public relations campaign: Budget for PR of event
Apply the PR campaign for event
Appreciate and develop a professional and critical attitude towards the job of public relations for event.

assessments.Grading Guide: Participation grade will be given based on students' preparation, and quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussion, and builds upon others’ comments. Class preparation and pre-reading before lecture will be assessed upon individuals' understanding and ability to answer questions in the class. Individuals will be called up randomly to be assessed.

assessments.Question Type: Part 1: Event PR campaign proposal Written report and presentation Option 1: Minimum length of the group assignment should be 10 pages, excluding appendices Option 2: Follow lecturer's proposal
assessments.No Question: Written report: PR campaign of an event. Presentation: 20 -25 mins/group
assessments.Grading Guide: In class and at home Task Description: Option 1: Students assume they are working for a public relations agency and responsible for creating a public relations campaign for an event such as: launch product, conference, charity event, exhibition or festival, sport event... , which must include a realistic strategy for a real-life event, Students will design, develop and evaluate a campaign for a “real” client. They will meet the client face-to-face, take a brief and be tasked with developing industry-ready materials for a public relations campaign. Or students will be provided with a list of current issues, and organisations linked to or impacted by those issues. From the list, they will select one issue and one organization to take care of. A campaign proposal for the client must include: Part 1: (1) Executive Summary (2) Situation Analysis (3) Target Audience and key stakeholders (4) Goal (5) Objectives (6) Key Messages Option 2: For Constructivism Approach only: Follow lecturer's proposal - Studying at the same time of EVN204. - Participating in implementation PR for EVN204.
assessments.Note: Students should illustrate excellent knowledge of public relations theories and how they can be applied. Critical skills in planning and execution of a public relations campaign also must be showed. The mark will be given based on each student's performance, not on the whole group's. It means each student will get their own mark.

assessments.Grading Guide: Option 1: Critical Essay At home Task Description: The critical essay is intended to help students identify basic concepts and principles of effective public relations by analysing a key development, change or issue applied to the field of PR and professional communication. Students will choose a topic, from the list provided, or they may provide a detailed topic of their own to be cleared in writing by the lecturer. The topics are intended to justify some of the themes covered in the course and provide them with the opportunity to gain their knowledge and examine how their topic impacts on society, publics, consumers and professional practice. Notes: Students should provide clear illustrations/examples in their essay to show their understanding of the topic. All topics are written as a draft. Lecturers have the privilege to change the content of each topic as much as they want. Choose one from the following essay topics: Topic 1: What are the pros and cons of using a celebrity as part of a promotional event? Topic 2: Describe the work of an entertainment publicist. Would you be interested in applying for the job of press coordinator? Topic 3: Why is it important for event executives to have a good relationship with the mass media? How can you as a PR professional facilitate that relationship? Option 2: (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal
